q: How does Horikita keep Ayanokouji from sleeping in class after the point system is revealed?
a: She stabs him in the right arm with her mathematical compass, warning that getting caught sleeping would undoubtedly cost points.

q: What study plan does Hirata announce to the class?
a: A study group meeting at five o'clock for two hours daily until the midterm, prepared with help from high-scoring students, open to anyone anxious about failing.

q: Which three failing students refuse to join Hirata's study group?
a: Sudou, Ike, and Yamauchi, held back by pride, jealousy of Hirata's popularity, and plans to cram the night before.

q: How does Horikita secure Ayanokouji's cooperation for recruiting the failures?
a: She treats him to an expensive special lunch set, then reveals it was not goodwill but an ulterior motive, leveraging his role in the cafe scheme and openly threatening him until he agrees.

q: What milestone does Ayanokouji reach during his deal with Horikita?
a: He receives a girl's contact information - hers - for the first time in his high school life, though he is not particularly happy about it.

q: How do Sudou and Ike each justify refusing the study group?
a: Sudou says he will cram the night before and has basketball club, while Ike waves it off mid-texting, claiming he could have scored forty points if not for the surprise test.

q: What absurd motivational incentives does Ayanokouji float to Horikita?
a: He suggests she promise to be their girlfriend or give them a kiss if they score perfectly; she responds by asking if he wants to die and jabbing him with something sharp.

q: Why does Ayanokouji decide Kushida is the perfect recruiter?
a: She is sociable with everyone regardless of gender, Ike is madly in love with her, Sudou and others have good impressions of her, and her own test scores are relatively high.

q: How does Kushida react when asked to gather students for the study group?
a: She hesitates only because she is happy, calls expulsion for bad grades cruel, admires that Horikita noticed the failing students, and eagerly volunteers to participate herself as well.

q: What rumor among the girls does Kushida reveal about Horikita and Ayanokouji?
a: That they might be dating, since Horikita only gets along well with him and they eat together; both deny anything romantic before exchanging numbers.

q: What condition does Horikita impose regarding Kushida and the study group?
a: Kushida may only help gather the students - she is absolutely not allowed to join the study group itself, since her grades were not failing.

q: How does Kushida respond when Ayanokouji cancels her involvement?
a: She stays eerily calm, deduces exactly what happened - that Horikita vetoed her membership rather than her gathering people - and asks him to leave everything to her.

q: Who does Kushida bring to the library study session?
a: Ike, Yamauchi, and Sudou, plus an unexpected addition: Okitani, a slender boy with a blue bob who scored thirty-nine and was too timid to join Hirata's group.

q: How does Kushida outmaneuver Horikita's ban on her joining the study group?
a: Having secured Okitani's admission first, she claims she barely passed the short test by guessing on multiple-choice questions and worries about failing too, leaving Horikita forced to growl 'Fine.'

q: What target score does Horikita set for the failing students?
a: Fifty points across the board, arguing that merely aiming at the thirty-two-point threshold is dangerous skating.

q: What is the first practice problem Horikita presents?
a: A simultaneous-equations word problem: A, B, and C collectively have 2,150 yen, A has 120 yen more than B, and after C gives B two-fifths of his money B would have 220 yen more than A - find A's original amount.

q: Why does the first library session collapse?
a: The failures cannot grasp simultaneous equations at all; Sudou quits outright, Horikita savagely insults everyone including his NBA dreams, Ike quits out of resentment, Yamauchi follows, and Okitani drifts out after them.

q: How far does Sudou go when enraged at Horikita in the library?
a: He slams the desk and grabs her by the collar, and Kushida has to grab his arm faster than Ayanokouji can move to stop violence.

q: What cold conclusion does Horikita reach after the study group falls apart?
a: That it is better to get rid of the dead weight - if the failing students are expelled, the class average rises and no extra effort is wasted.

q: What does Kushida whisper before leaving the defeated study group?
a: That she is going to do something, she will try, and she definitely does not want everything to fall apart so quickly because she does not want to abandon the three boys.

q: What does Ayanokouji witness on the rooftop staircase?
a: Through a crack in the door he sees Kushida alone, venting in a low voice unlike her own - calling someone seriously annoying, saying it would be better if she just died, and cursing Horikita as a rotten harpy.

q: How does Kushida react to being overheard?
a: She turns ice-cold, pins him against the wall with a forearm, threatens that if he tells anyone she will claim he raped her, and forces his palm against her breast to plant fingerprint evidence on her unwashed uniform.

q: What does Kushida say motivates her two-faced behavior?
a: Wanting everyone to like her - she says that is what she wants out of life and gives her existence meaning, while admitting she absolutely despises gloomy, ordinary guys like Ayanokouji.

q: What timeline hole does Ayanokouji expose about Kushida?
a: She learned Ayanokouji's name from his self-introduction, yet knew Horikita's name before Horikita had introduced herself to anyone - suggesting they knew each other or attended the same school in the past; Kushida visibly shudders.

q: What evidence does Kushida cite that Ayanokouji is indifferent to other people?
a: That back on the bus on the first day, he showed no interest in giving up his seat to the elderly woman.

q: How does Kushida behave immediately after threatening Ayanokouji?
a: She kicks his thigh hard in anger, then instantly switches back to her sunny self and brightly suggests heading back together, like Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde.

q: What bullying talk emerges in the guys' group chat after Satou joins?
a: Members discuss hitting Horikita, completely ignoring her, or hiding her shoes to make her cry; Ayanokouji declares neutrality but warns the school punishes bullying and that Kushida would hate them for it.

q: What reflection does Ayanokouji have while watching the chat drama unfold?
a: He feels detached, drifting past a crisis that should concern him, and recalls Chiyabashira's words that only a fool would not use his innate abilities.

q: Who does Ayanokouji discover Horikita meeting late at night outside the dorms?
a: Student council president Horikita Manabu - her older brother, whom she addresses as niisan.

q: What does Horikita Manabu demand of his younger sister?
a: He tells her coming to this school was a mistake, insists she will never reach Class A, says her class will fall apart, and orders her to leave the school immediately so his standing is not humiliated.

q: How does the confrontation between Manabu and Ayanokouji turn physical?
a: After Ayanokouji pulls him off Suzune, Manabu attempts a backhand and a sharp kick with knockout power; Ayanokouji evades all blows quickly and slaps his hand away, prompting Manabu to ask whether he has been taught.

q: What cover story does Ayanokouji give for his reflexes?
a: He claims he was taught piano and calligraphy and won a national music competition in elementary school; later he adds tea ceremony to the list.

q: What martial arts credentials does Horikita credit her brother with?
a: He is ranked fifth dan in karate and fourth dan in aikido.

q: What does Manabu say about Ayanokouji as he leaves?
a: That Suzune has an unusual classmate, and that with Ayanokouji around things might get interesting.

q: What argument does Ayanokouji make against letting the failing students be expelled?
a: That the school might levy unseen penalties for expulsions - possibly enormous point deductions - and since every individual has strengths and weaknesses, discarding them risks disaster for everyone's future.

q: How does Ayanokouji use Chiyabashira's own words against Horikita's worldview?
a: He quotes her guidance-room line asking who decided smart people are categorically superior, concluding academics do not solely determine rankings.

q: What flaw does Ayanokouji name in Horikita Suzune?
a: That she considers everyone else a burden, detaches herself, and never lets anyone close - which may be the very reason she was placed in Class D.

q: On what condition does Horikita finally agree to protect the failing students?
a: Strictly for her own sake - as a strategic means of securing future advantage - and Ayanokouji reflects that he has made a deal with the devil.

q: Why did Horikita originally propose a study group if she despises helping others?
a: Ayanokouji reasons she must have already considered the risk of unknown penalties for expulsions - otherwise she would simply have abandoned the failures from the beginning.
